svg.title: Six Layer 2 technologies, the separate problem each one solves, and the point where each one locks onto the others
svg.desc: Six rows. STP stops loops by blocking ports and therefore decides every path. VLAN splits broadcast and failure domain and sets the scope STP must compute over. Trunk carries many VLANs on one link and can silently bridge two VLANs through a native VLAN mismatch. Link aggregation adds bandwidth and link redundancy, and because STP sees one logical link it removes a blocked port. Clustering removes STP blocking entirely and moves the single point to the peer link. FHRP provides gateway redundancy and must sit on the same switch as the root bridge. A note at the bottom says VLAN, STP and FHRP are three presentations of one decision: the scope, the path and the exit.
svg.text: Six technologies, not six topics: each one changes the premises of the others
Read the third column as the contract each feature signs with the rest of the design
TECHNOLOGY
THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES, ALONE
WHERE IT LOCKS ONTO THE OTHERS
STP
loop prevention
Stops loops by blocking ports — so it decides
every path anyone will ever use.
Whatever a VLAN spans is what STP must compute over.
Enlarge the VLAN and you enlarge the calculation and the blast radius.
VLAN
broadcast and failure domain
Splits one switch into several broadcast domains
without buying a switch per domain.
Sets the scope for STP, the subnet plan and the FHRP groups.
VLAN 1 quietly carries everything nobody assigned.
Trunk
many VLANs, one link
Carries many VLANs between switches over
one physical interface.
A native VLAN mismatch bridges two VLANs with no error at all.
The allowed list decides what can leak where.
Link aggregation
bandwidth, link redundancy
Adds bandwidth and removes single-link failure
using links you already paid for.
STP sees one logical link, so it silently removes a blocked port.
min-links turns a degraded bundle into a deliberate outage.
Clustering
vPC, MLAG, stacking
Removes STP blocking between two switches,
so both uplinks forward.
Moves the single point from the link to the peer link,
and adds a new failure mode that needs its own detection.
FHRP
gateway redundancy
Keeps a default gateway reachable when one
device or uplink fails.
Must sit on the same switch as the STP root, or every
packet crosses the core link and comes back.
Three of the six are one decision seen from three angles: the VLAN sets the scope, STP sets the path, FHRP sets the exit.
Configured by three people in three change windows, they contradict. Configured as one decision, the rest of this chapter is detail.
The other three — trunk, aggregation, clustering — are the levers that alter what the first three are allowed to assume.
